newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares soften as market takes a breather.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares soften as market takes a breather.

text.p: Leading Russian shares slipped on Monday in quiet, low-volume trade as investors took a breather after recent highs. Dealers forecast that lethargic market conditions would continue in the next few days.
The Russian Trading System 22-share index closed 0.67 percent down on Monday at 418.63 from 421.46 at the close on Friday.
"The market is consolidating after the dramatic gains of the last week, " said Brunswick director Martin Diggle.

LUKoil ordinaries edged down to $19.4 from $19.7 at Friday's close, while LUKoil preferred fell to $12.60 from $13.25. National power utility UES edged up to $0.3614 from $0.3611 and utility Mosenergo was $1.397 after $1.415.
Alfa-Capital chief trader Mikhail Khaleyev said the market was fluctuating in a narrow trading range, mainly on Russian operators' activity.
"I think the market will consolidate...I do not expect any dramatic moves up or down," Diggle said.
Results of Gazprom's annual shareholders' meeting on Saturday had little impact on the market, traders said.
The gas monopoly said it had changed some of its rules on trade in its shares, including the scrapping of a charter clause saying only nine percent of the company could be sold to foreigners.
But a presidential decree limiting foreign ownership to nine percent remains in force.
Western buyers therefore should not think Gazprom was going to offer more shares, traders said.
"I think the news at the AGM was nothing really sensational, and in line with what people were expecting," Diggle said.
News that oil company SIDANKO plans an American Depositary Receipts issue in early 1998 and a convertible bond later this year failed to affect the market either, traders said.
SIDANKO production units include Kondpetroleum, Varyoganneftegaz and Chernogorneft.
